title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', which continues La Longue Marche. He studies the 'loop equation' for automorphisms of the profinite group π̂_{0,3}, extended by complex conjugation σ_∞. This is the setting later formalised by Drinfeld and Ihara as the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. Here he analyses its shadow in SL(2,Ẑ), the case h=1.

Data from the previous page:
- α₀ = (a b; c d) and f = (r s; t u), with entries in Ẑ. The determinant of α₀ is δ = ±1 and det f = 1.
- ξ = α₀ ρ(α₀)^{-1} = (A B; C D), where ρ is the order-3 symmetry. Its entries are quadratic expressions. For example δD = c²+cd+d², the Eisenstein norm form, and the relation C+D−B = 1 holds (54).
- φ = f σ_∞(f)^{-1} = f·ᵗf = (R S; T U). Here R = r²+s², S = T = rt+su and U = t²+u² (Gaussian norm forms), so φ is symmetric (55).
- The loop equation (56) is ξ = ε ρ₀^ν φ with ε = ±1. Here ρ₀^ν is a unipotent upper-triangular matrix (1 ±2ν; 0 1), the image of a power of the order-2 generator in Γ(2). The integer ν ∈ Ẑ plays the role of Drinfeld's m = (λ−1)/2.

This page.
- (57) writes the equation entrywise as (A+2νC, B+2νD; C, D) = ε(R, S; T=S, U).
- Symmetry of the right side forces C = B+2νD, so 2νD = C−B. By (54), C−B = 1−D. Hence (2ν+1)D = 1, i.e. (58) μD = 1 with μ = 2ν+1. In particular μ and D are units in Ẑ.
- Symmetrically, he inverts the equation: A = ε(R−2νT), B = ε(S−2νU), C = εT, D = εU. Substituting into C+D−B = 1 gives T+U−S+2νU = ε. Since S = T this is (59) μU = ε.
- Combined with (58) this gives (60) D = εU, which is just equality of the lower-right entries in (57).

Upshot (made explicit as a Théorème on the next page). The multiplier μ, the analogue of Drinfeld's λ (the cyclotomic character), is determined by ξ through μ^{-1} = D = δ(c²+cd+d²). Up to sign it is also determined by φ through μ^{-1} = ε(t²+u²). So μ^{-1} must be represented, up to sign, both by the norm form of Z[ζ₃] (from the order-3 relation) and by the norm form of Z[i] (from the order-2 relation), over Ẑ.

The next page also self-corrects a dimension count of the solution scheme over Spec Z, from relative dimension 3 to 4.
errors: No algebraic error on this page: both derivations, μD=1 and μU=ε, check out given (54) and S=T.
Sign conventions are loose. The page writes A+2νC, i.e. multiplication by ρ₀^{+ν}, while (56) on the previous page is rearranged as ρ₀^{-ν}ξ = εφ. This is immaterial for the conclusions.
The previous page's (48) 'ab−cd' should presumably be the determinant ad−bc (likely a transcription or slip issue).

ideas.what: Reducing the loop (hexagon-type) equation to the congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ) ⊃ Γ(2)^ and extracting the multiplier μ = 2ν+1 from a single matrix entry (μD=1).
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-type elements (λ,f) under π̂_{0,3} → Γ̂(2) ⊂ SL₂(Ẑ); λ = cyclotomic character, m=(λ−1)/2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT and λ; Ihara (late 1980s–90s) for the Galois / profinite free group setting
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and Galois action; this computation is not there

ideas.what: μ^{-1} represented by both x²+xy+y² (from the order-3 relation) and x²+y² (from the order-2 relation via f·ᵗf) over Ẑ.
ideas.modern_name: Norm forms of Z[ζ₃] and Z[i] appearing in the 2- and 3-cycle relations of GT at abelian/matrix level
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (implicit in analyses of GT's image in GL₂)

missed.claim: An explicit 'SL₂ shadow' of Grothendieck's loop equation. It shows the multiplier μ (Drinfeld's λ) is read off as the inverse of an Eisenstein-norm entry of α₀ρ(α₀)^{-1}, and up to sign as the inverse of a Gaussian-norm entry of f·ᵗf. This is a small but concrete trace of Grothendieck's independent pre-Drinfeld handling of the λ-parameter.
missed.quote: 2νD = 1−D i.e. μD = 1 ... μ = 2ν+1, ce qui implique déjà μ et D inversibles ... (59) μU = ε
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that Grothendieck worked with the parameter ν ≈ m = (λ−1)/2 and with the order-2/order-3 relations at the congruence-matrix level. The mathematics itself is elementary and consistent with what is known about GT's image in Ẑ^*.

deep.surprise_reason: The computations are correct but elementary linear algebra. Their interest is historical: Grothendieck's own parametrisation of the cyclotomic multiplier in the loop equation, in an unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche. There is no new result a specialist would find surprising.
transcription_corrections: The crossed-out passage reads approximately 'D'autre part, on doit avoir écrit (57)', replaced by 'symétriquement, si on écrit (57) sous la forme'. The left-hand side of the displayed equation carries a factor ε in front of (A B; C D).
In (58) the second relation appears to read 'μ^{-1} = 1/D' (or 'μ = 1/D'). A crossed-out fragment precedes 'i.e. D = 1/μ'.
Last line: probably 'l'égalité des termes droits inférieurs des matrices (57)', i.e. the lower-right entries (D = εU), rather than 'deux lignes inférieures'.
In (59) the second relation is written 'μ = ε/U' with a small subscript (possibly φ) under the equals sign.
